text:
Ivy: Quick thread  need a one-page battlecard for the launch focused on infra buyers. Must be punchy for slide deck + handout.
Marcus: Agreed. Audience = platform architects + procurement. Keep to 3 counterclaims, 2 metrics, one memorable metaphor, and exact inbound routing tags.
Talia: My starter counters: 1) Predictable serving beats benchmark peaks. 2) Unit economics matter more than broad model catalogs. 3) Deployment parity removes go-live risk. Each should be one line.
Rohit: For metrics we can show: 30d p99 on reserved pools (seq=512) and sustained throughput at long contexts (seq=1024). Ops snapshot will back it.
Ivy: Metaphor idea: "Models are instruments; Redwood is the conductor and the score it keeps timing consistent even when the orchestra changes." Short and evocative.
Marcus: Love it  different from the airline/road metaphors. For inbound routing, propose tags: `lead_tier=enterprise|mid|selfserve`, `capacity_sensitive=true|false`, `compliance=none|std|high`. Map enterprise+capacity->AE+SolutionsEng; compliance=high->SecuritySE cc.
Talia: Good. Salesops wants exact field names. Use the strings above and include them in the PR to forms.
sales-bot: Suggested form fields created draft: `lead_tier`, `capacity_sensitive`, `compliance`. PR: https://git.redwood/forms/pull/2048.
Rohit: Ops snapshot: ms-2026-299123 p99=127ms (seq=512, dedicated), sustained tps=19 (seq=1024). Will attach link in the footnote.
Ivy: For visible copy avoid jargon like "KV cache". Use "response caching" and "continuous batching" in the footnote only. Visible copy must be customer-facing.
Marcus: Rebut line vs cloud vendors who tout "instant scale": "Burst scale is not the same as predictable SLAs peaks cost you and your users." One line.
Talia: We'll also add a micro-case: anonymized SaaS win  checkout latency improved after reserved capacity + batching. Keep it one sentence and cite internal ticket.
Rohit: Canary policy callout: 2-hour 5% canary with latency/error thresholds. Short ops sentence on battlecard and link to policy in footnote.
Ivy: Draft timeline: first-pass by noon, review in 2pm sync, finalize for slides by 5pm. Draft location: https://git.redwood/marketing/webinar-assets/conductor-battlecard-draft.md
Marcus: I'll assemble the initial bullets and routing table. Talia, please write the metaphor box and the CTAs. Rohit, paste the perf links and ticket IDs.
Talia: CTA language suggestion: enterprise -> "Request a predictable pilot" ; others -> "Start free trial". Keep button copy short.
Rohit: Adding footnotes: perf snapshot link, anonymized ticket INT-6782, canary policy path /infra/policies/canary-guidelines.md, cost explainer page.
Ivy: One more: keep surface area to one page. No percent claims without a linked study. Use "reduces per-token spend through batching and response caching" instead of a percent.
Marcus: Noted. I'll avoid hard percent claims.
Talia: I'll proofread tone for customer-facing clarity after initial draft.
Ivy: Thanks team  post the draft link here when done and tag salesops for the form wiring.
Marcus: Draft posted: https://git.redwood/marketing/webinar-assets/conductor-battlecard-draft.md. Please review before 2pm.
Rohit: Perf links added to the doc and snapshot posted to #eng-metrics.
Ivy: Great work. We'll iterate in PR.
